REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - NOVEMBER 14, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Invocation
The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.
Invocation
3.

Pledge of Allegiance
4.

5.
Presentations/Appointments
5A.
Presentations
Presentations
6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
October 24, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes
7B.
Approval of Registers of Demands
7B.1.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 14, 2019 (COUNCIL).
City Register
7B.2.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency dated November 14, 2019 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Agency Register
7C.
Approval of Treasurer's Reports
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending September 30, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Treasurer's Reports
7D.
Adoption of Ordinance
Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of October 24, 2019:
Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1028, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 5.35 AND CHAPTER 22.40 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE SALE OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-5 (COUNCIL).*
*Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.
Agenda Report
8.
Public Hearings
8A.
Review and consideration of a written appeal of a decision of the Property Preservation Commission denying a request to remove a parkway tree adjacent to the property located at 13558 Felson Street, Cerritos, California (APN 7023-002-055), Property Preservation Commission Case No. TR 2019-03 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
8B.
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS, ANTICIPATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY $209,325, TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO EXERCISE EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT EL RANCHO VERDE PARK (FITNESS STATIONS) AND LIBERTY PARK (FIT CORE) (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9.
New and Old Business
9A.
Review and consideration of award of a contract for printing and mailing of the Cerritos News, Cerritos Library News & Cerritos Lifelong Enrichment Combined Newsletter, and Community Services Program, Bid No. 1391-19 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9B.
Review and consideration of award of a contract for fire alarm system replacement for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, Project No. 12716, Bid No. 1390-19 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
10.
Legislative Items
10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
NOVEMBER 14, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Teen
  Volunteer Hana Sandomirsky.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Janelle Paule, Korean American Family Services, spoke regarding the hazards of
  second-hand smoke. She submitted documents for the record.

  Karen Wilson spoke regarding Neighborhood Watch Zone 54 activities, including
  home decorating events, and encouraged other Neighborhood Watch Zones to add
  holiday events in their Zones.

  Roger Kline inquired as to the requirements to place an item on the ballot and spoke
  regarding health benefits for the City Council.

  Herman exercised his first amendment rights to free speech and spoke regarding
  homeless issues. He submitted a document for the record.

  Artellia Johnson spoke regarding the lease of the Mullikin Building. She submitted a
  document for the record.
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  October 24, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of October 24, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 14,
  2019 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register
  of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  11/14/2019  $10,358,158.20 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated November 14, 2019 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register
  of Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  11/14/2019  $14,346,943.82 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period
  ending September 30, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending September 30,
  2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of October 24, 2019:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1028, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 5.35 AND CHAPTER 22.40 OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE SALE OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES
  IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE
  AMENDMENT 2019-5 (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar by Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama,
  for separate consideration by the City Council.

  A staff report was provided by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Janelle Paule noted the hazards of smoking in outdoor areas.

  Herman spoke about the hazards of smoking, e-cigarettes, and vaping.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the
  public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to waive full reading
  of and adopt Ordinance No. 1028, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 5.35 AND CHAPTER 22.40 OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE SALE OF ELECTRONIC
  CIGARETTES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-5 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of a written appeal of a decision of the Property
  Preservation Commission denying a request to remove a parkway tree adjacent to
  the property located at 13558 Felson Street, Cerritos, California (APN 7023-002-
  055), Property Preservation Commission Case No. TR 2019-03 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Karen Wilson, appellant, expressed concerns for her health due to the falling pine
  cones and noted the tree roots are causing sidewalk damage.

  Herman expressed concerns regarding mitigation measures for tree-related
  damage.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the
  public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the
  appeal of a decision of the Cerritos Property Preservation Commission denying a
  request to remove one parkway tree adjacent to the property located at 13558
  Felson Street, Cerritos, California, 90703 (APN 7023-002-055), and noting the
  subject tree will be removed (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Edwards, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS, ANTICIPATED TO
  BE APPROXIMATELY $209,325, TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO EXERCISE
  EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT EL RANCHO VERDE PARK (FITNESS STATIONS) AND
  LIBERTY PARK (FIT CORE) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Herman spoke regarding the importance of accessibility in public areas.

  Noting there were no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public
  hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2019-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS, ANTICIPATED
  TO BE APPROXIMATELY $209,325, TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO
  EXERCISE EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT EL RANCHO VERDE PARK (FITNESS
  STATIONS) AND LIBERTY PARK (FIT CORE) (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for printing and mailing of the
  Cerritos News, Cerritos Library News & Cerritos Lifelong Enrichment Combined
  Newsletter, and Community Services Program, Bid No. 1391-19 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to award a contract for
  printing and mailing of the Cerritos News, Cerritos Library News & Cerritos Lifelong
  Enrichment Combined Newsletter, and Community Services Program, Bid No. 1391-
  19, to Southwest Offset Printing in the amount of $60,774.29. In the event issues of
  non-performance arise, the project would be removed from Southwest Offset Printing
  and taken to the next lowest qualified bidder to ensure the City’s printing deadline,
  quality standards and specifications are met. This process would be repeated as
  necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for fire alarm system replacement
  for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, Project No. 12716, Bid No. 1390-19
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Reject the sole bid received for the replacement of the fire alarm system at the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts; and

  2. Authorize staff to re-advertise the project at a future date (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards and Hu, Mayor Pro Tem
  Yokoyama, and Mayor Solanki.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to direct staff to
  provide an update report in an upcoming Closed Session regarding the recent
  litigation with AFSCME (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Edwards, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Direct staff to place an information report on an
  upcoming agenda regarding the use of “Roundup” products.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to
  direct staff to place a report on an upcoming agenda to consider the City’s use of
  social media (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not pass (2 - 3) as follows:

  AYES:  Pulido, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Edwards, Hu, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  November 14, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 8:59 p.m.
